provider_boundary: Backend never constructs provider transports or credentials. All actual model execution, cancellation, status and event reads use the authenticated canonical EngineClient.

routes.send: POST /api/ai/chat: canonical conversation and user idempotency key; response_mode wait/deferred/stream
routes.probe: GET /api/ai/chat/turns/{thread_id}?idempotency_key=...; commits terminal engine result to canonical conversation
routes.cancel: POST /api/ai/chat/turns/{thread_id}/cancel: explicit canonical cancellation; terminal truth wins
routes.models: GET /api/ai/models: authenticated canonical engine inventory projection
routes.resume: POST /api/ai/chat/turns/{thread_id}/resume {idempotency_key,response_mode?}: reuse original server-prepared command and deadline, no caller reconstruction

request: provider_id/model_id are optional exact registered engine catalog identities, attachment_refs are authorized canonical references, max_output_tokens is bounded and temperature finite. Selection and attachment identities bind durable user-message retry provenance. Browser-supplied conversation history is rejected.
context: Canonical active transcript is authoritative; the instruction policy stays trusted_control/mandatory. Latest user message, requested attachments and explicit code context keep their data trust levels and must survive compilation with exact ID/hash, or admission rejects before a fresh user commit. Recent history is bounded100 messages/512KiB, selected runtime budgets and complete rendered local input are checked, and no unbounded parallel history is sent.

sse.source: Durable engine execution events, with original event_id/sequence and execution lineage validated before forwarding
sse.resume: Nonnegative canonical engine sequence cursor, explicit after_sequence or numeric Last-Event-ID; gaps require resynchronization rather than fabricated deltas
sse.engine_events: event: engine.<canonical type>; data: safe canonical event record; id: original sequence
sse.final: event: chat.final; canonical turn payload only after assistant or terminal conversation receipt commits; final projection is idempotent and may repeat after reconnect
sse.failure: event: chat.error or chat.resync_required with stable safe code/retryability and polling recovery hint
sse.detach: Client disconnection detaches delivery and preserves canonical work; explicit cancellation is a separate command

finalization: Durable engine result, recovered context handoff and exact canonical turn identity must agree before idempotent assistant commit. Failed/cancelled execution produces a system-derived terminal marker and never fabricated assistant success.
errors: Safe stable application errors distinguish authorization, conversation/version conflict, admission/capacity, engine unavailable, execution failure, provider protocol and finalization unavailable; raw prompts, credentials and transport exceptions are not returned.
verification_policy_this_session: User explicitly requested implementation only and NO TESTS; no tests are written or run for this wave. This contract records implementation intent and does not manufacture acceptance or closure evidence.
prepared_admission: Fresh server-assigned user UUID/time, exact compiled EngineExecutionCommand and source/request identities are admitted and committed together in the existing recoverable prepared Mongo message row. First committed writer wins; backend re-reads the frozen command before submission. Edited and older unprepared USER tips can bind command metadata once. GET missingengine reports awaiting_admission/acceptedfalse/server_resume_available. Expired command cannot receive a new deadline; backend reprobes canonical admission and returns explicit expired/unconfirmed if still absent. A point-in-time404 never manufactures a durable failed/cancelled receipt. Original command remains for canonical status reconciliation.
classification: Each new user and prepared command preserves the maximum source/policy/ancestor classification. Engine handoff cannot fall below thread/user/internal policy floor; assistant message commits at actual engine binding class. Higher-class source data is never downgraded to a lower thread label.
source_withdrawal: Current attachment rights/bytes are rechecked before fresh dispatch, incomplete resumption and every streaming heartbeat; deadlines cannot exceed sourceexpiry. Unavailable sources trigger best-effort canonical cancellation and safe delivery denial. Already-transferred data and historical engine context/result copies cannot be unsent or claimed erased by attachment-only removal.
product_facade: EngineChat/EngineText propagate exact registered provider/model and optional supported temperature, reject silently ignored parameters, bound history/evidence/prompt bytes and serialize turns. Explicit turn retries use one bounded completed projection and exact request semantics; new prompt source identity binds options/context through canonical handoff.
validation_performed: Source-only review, Python AST parsing, Black formatting and Ruff checking. No tests were written or run, as expressly instructed; no behavior/closure evidence is claimed.
